# Ness (ness.city)

> The civic layer for builders: open-source tooling that turns a community's problems into bounties into shipped fixes.

Ness is a portfolio of small, opinionated tools for community-driven cities. The core loop lives in Townhall: anyone files a problem with a real diagnosis, the community refines the root cause, a citizen proposes a concrete fix, patrons crowdfund it in USDC on Base, and a solver ships it, earning karma, the bounty, and permanent attribution for the patrons. Alongside Townhall it runs Jobs (hand-curated public openings), PageRank (a social ranking that surfaces who a city named most), and Pulse (community stats), with Match and Market on the roadmap.

It is for ambitious builders inside network communities who want latent problems made legible and routed to whoever can actually fix them. The repo is public and open-source (MIT). This is an independent project, not affiliated with Network School.

## Key links
- [Home](https://ness.city/): overview of Ness and its tools for community-driven cities.
- [Townhall](https://ness.city/townhall): the five-step engine where problems become bounties become shipped fixes.
- [PageRank](https://ness.city/pagerank): map your ring in doubling rounds; social ranking surfaces who the city named most.
- [Guide](https://ness.city/guide): how the system works and how to take part.
- [Roadmap](https://ness.city/roadmap): what is live, in design, and planned.
- [Pulse](https://ness.city/pulse): community stats and activity.
